en: Like, I'll give you a story.
zh: 比如说,我给你讲个故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, there were a bunch of really smart venture firms doing the dot-com boom that got in in 93, 94, made money, and decided to step out of the game in 96, 97.
zh: 在互联网泡沫时期,有一批非常聪明的风投公司在 93、94 年入场,赚了钱,然后在 96、97 年决定退出这个游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when they stepped out of the game, they missed out on 97, 98, 99.
zh: 而当他们退出游戏后,他们错过了 97、98、99 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the LPs were like, what happened?
zh: 而且 LP 们就问，发生了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: We asked you.
zh: 我们问过你。

speaker: Unknown
en: We invested in you because you're going to be at the cutting edge.
zh: 我们投资你是因为你将处于最前沿。

speaker: Unknown
en: You stepped out.
zh: 你退出了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they stepped back in 2000.
zh: 而他们在 2000 年又杀了回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So timing markets is really, really hard.
zh: 所以择时市场真的、真的非常难。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you have to play the game.
zh: 我认为你必须参与这个游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think you can play the game differently.
zh: 但我认为你可以用不同的方式参与这个游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can choose to be more selective.
zh: 你可以选择更有选择性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can hopefully think about portfolio composition and position sizing as a way of mitigating what happens in the cycle turns.
zh: 而且你可以有希望地把投资组合构成和仓位规模作为一种缓解周期逆转时会发生什么的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Portfolio composition and position sizing.
zh: 投资组合构成和仓位规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do we do with both of those in a market then like this?
zh: 在这样的市场里，我们对这两者要做些什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we change them?
zh: 我们如何改变它们？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you have to think about the venture portfolio as a bunch of options.
zh: 我认为你必须把风险投资组合看作一堆期权。

speaker: Unknown
en: Each seed investment is an option bet.
zh: 每一笔种子投资都是一个期权下注。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're buying an option to see if it's an outlier.
zh: 你在买一个期权，来看它是不是个离群值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you want to have enough of those so you can make sure you have an outlier.
zh: 所以你要有足够多的这种期权，这样你才能确保自己拿到一个离群值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then when there are true quantitative evidence based on revenue on quantifiable metrics that there's going to be an outlier, then you position size up.
zh: 然后当有真正的基于收入的定量证据、基于可量化指标的证据表明它会成为离群值时，你就加大仓位。

speaker: Unknown
en: So to me, you have to think about, okay, what is my fund size?
zh: 对我来说，你必须想清楚，好的，我的基金规模是多少？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do I have enough at-bats, to use a baseball analogy?
zh: 我怎么才有足够的击球次数，用棒球来打个比方？

speaker: Unknown
en: And make sure that you have enough at-bats, and then you only position size up on the things that are already proven.
zh: 确保你有足够的击球次数，然后你只对那些已经被证明的东西加大仓位。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think seed still really exists today?
zh: 你认为种子轮今天还真的存在吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you want to go into the core AI world with the neo labs, I think seed is hard.
zh: 如果你想进入核心 AI 世界、进入那些 neo 实验室，我认为种子轮很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: But even AI application companies, they're raising 10 to 20.
zh: 但即便是 AI 应用公司，它们也在融 10 到 20。

speaker: Unknown
en: The old three to five days, which were still quite large seeds, and that's gone.
zh: 以前的三到五 days，那已经算是很大的种子轮了，而那个已经消失了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Honestly, I think there are two things that impact seed investing today.
zh: 老实说，我认为今天有两件事在影响种子投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is the size of the round.
zh: 一是轮次规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you have this other sort of externality, which is these large funds, maybe including us, somewhat being indifferent to seed valuations because they're using that as an option check.
zh: 然后还有另一种外部性，就是这些大型基金，也许包括我们在内，某种程度上对种子轮估值无所谓，因为它们把那当作一张期权支票。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because you are, aren't you?
zh: 因为你就是这样，不是吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I didn't mean that to put you on the spot, but...
zh: 我没想让你难堪，但是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we are trying to buy ourselves a seat at the table, and the cost of buying that seat at the table we are somewhat indifferent to at the stage stage because our real goal is to size up and invest in them if they become outliers.
zh: 我是说，我们是在试图给自己买个席位，而在这个阶段买这个席位的成本我们某种程度上是无所谓的，因为我们真正的目标是在它们成为离群值时加大仓位并投资它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for making my life harder in that respect.
zh: 谢谢你在这方面让我日子更难过。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should just invest in our funds.
zh: 你应该直接投资我们的基金。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's very funny.
zh: 那真有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nicely transitioned there.
zh: 那里过渡得很漂亮。

speaker: Unknown
en: I give you credit for that one.
zh: 这一点我给你加分。

speaker: Unknown
en: You said you place these bets, so to speak, and then when you see discernible traction, then you can double down.
zh: 你说你下了这些赌注，可以这么说，然后当你看到可辨识的牵引力时，你就可以加倍下注。

speaker: Unknown
en: Completely agree with that logic.
zh: 完全同意这个逻辑。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're seeing strange numbers.
zh: 我们看到了一些奇怪的数字。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, contracted annual revenue that's not actually annual revenue and it's kind of not live.
zh: 你知道的，合同年度收入其实并不是真正的年度收入，而且某种程度上还没上线。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're seeing revenue run rate that's kind of extrapolated out from the best day in history and then we times that by 365 days.
zh: 你会看到收入运行率某种程度上是从史上最好的一天外推出来，然后我们再乘以 365 天。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a murkiness to this revenue that we've never seen before that makes me feel quite icky in a lot of cases.
zh: 这种收入有一种我们从未见过的模糊性，在很多情况下让我觉得相当恶心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you share that and how would you advise me and what do internal discussions look like around that?
zh: 你有同感吗？你会怎么建议我？内部讨论围绕这个是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: If any metric is measured by an investor and they put a lot of weight on it, it's going to be gamed.
zh: 如果任何指标被投资者衡量并且他们非常看重它，那它就一定会被钻空子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's just the nature.
zh: 这就是本性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe they should coin a law for it.
zh: 也许他们应该为此创造一个定律。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are two elements that are going on.
zh: 这里面有两个因素在起作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: One, I'm blanking, I don't know if it's Keynes or another famous economist who's coined the term bezel.
zh: 一，我一时想不起来，不知道是凯恩斯还是另一位著名经济学家创造了 bezel 这个词。

speaker: Unknown
en: When there's a boom, the bezel is high, which means it's a notion that the embezzlement of things will be.
zh: 当出现繁荣时，bezel 很高，这意味着它是一种 notion，即侵占 Things 的行为将会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: So not just people are going to pick metrics, people are also going to have some interesting accounting techniques, which, by the way, will happen every cycle.
zh: 所以不只是有人会挑选指标，人们还会有一些有趣的会计技巧，顺便说一句，这种情况每个周期都会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's probably happening at this cycle.
zh: 而且它很可能正在这个周期发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're going to find out in the next few years exactly the accounting creativity of some of our founders.
zh: 所以未来几年我们会确切地看到我们一些创始人的会计创造力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the metrics being gamed by some other people, right?
zh: 还有一些其他人在操弄指标，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: One good example of it in doing the SaaS way was a lot of investors put a lot of weight on net revenue retention.
zh: 在做 SaaS 那一套时，一个很好的例子是很多投资者非常看重净收入留存率。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so one of the ways to gain net revenue retention is that you could get a $100 PO, but better get a $10 PO and get a $50 PO a week later, because your net revenue retention, we just got a $100 PO was 100%.
zh: 于是提高净收入留存率的方法之一是，你可以拿到一张 100 美元的 PO，但最好先拿一张 10 美元的 PO，一周后再拿一张 50 美元的 PO，因为你刚拿到那张 100 美元的 PO 时，净收入留存率是 100%。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you got the $10 PO and the $50 PO, it's now 500%.
zh: 如果你先拿 10 美元的 PO 再拿 50 美元的 PO，那就变成 500% 了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the net revenue retention looks much better.
zh: 净收入留存率看起来就好多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once a metric is measured, it can be gamed.
zh: 一旦一个指标被度量，它就可以被操弄。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that happens.
zh: 而且这确实会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: To me, a lot of this comes down to, are the founders really focused on building a business?
zh: 对我来说，这一切很大程度上归结为：这些创始人是不是真的专注于打造一门生意？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are they focused on terminal value or they are focused on markups?
zh: 他们是专注于终端价值，还是专注于估值上调（markup）？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think you want to find founders and investors who are focused on terminal value.
zh: 我认为你要找的是专注于终端价值的创始人和投资者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you believe in kingmaking?
zh: 你相信“造王”（kingmaking）吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I know that sounds like a strange question, making the theory that multiple successive and quick rounds led by strong investors can really help increase the chances of a company being successful.
zh: 我知道这听起来像个奇怪的问题，这个理论是说由强势投资者连续主导的多轮快速融资确实能提高一家公司成功的概率。

speaker: Unknown
en: See, to me, that is a great example of Solos' reflexivity.
zh: 你看，对我来说，这正是索罗斯反身性的一个绝佳例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I mean by that is you have a company that does well, and because it does well and the revenue is growing really fast, it has a quick markup.
zh: 我的意思是，你有一家公司做得很好，因为它做得好、收入增长非常快，它就有了快速的估值上调。

speaker: Unknown
en: And because of that quick markup, it gets more capital, it gets to come on Harry's show, and then it gets more notoriety that allows you to get more human capital along to the financial capital.
zh: 而且正因为这次快速上调，它拿到更多资本，能上 Harry 的节目，然后获得更多知名度，这让你能在金融资本之外吸引更多人力资本。

speaker: Unknown
en: It grows faster, and that's another markup.
zh: 它增长得更快，又是一次估值上调。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, these are good things as long as the revenue is happening and the core business is building.
zh: 现在，只要收入是真的在发生、核心业务是真的在建立，这些都是好事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But someone, a copycat can look at that and say, oh, the secret is to have a markup.
zh: 但有人，一个模仿者，会看着这一套说：哦，秘诀就是估值上调。

speaker: Unknown
en: A copycat investor might look at it and say, if it's marked up, it's going to be marked up again.
zh: 一个模仿型投资者可能会看着它说：如果它上调过一次，它就会再次上调。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then reflexivity kicks in.
zh: 然后反身性就启动了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then everybody starts acting that way.
zh: 然后所有人都开始照这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this explains how market cycles work until it stops.
zh: 这就解释了市场周期是如何运转的，直到它停止。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one thing we know from Soros is that all reflexivity will eventually stop.
zh: 而我们从索罗斯那里知道的一件事是，所有反身性最终都会停止。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just don't know how and when.
zh: 我们只是不知道会以什么方式、在什么时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: But until it stops, a lot of people can look very smart.
zh: 但在它停止之前，很多人可以看起来非常聪明。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't know how and when, but we can play the game of predicting how and when.
zh: 我们不知道会以什么方式、在什么时候，但我们可以玩预测方式和时机的游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you were to predict how, what is the first signs of this cracking?
zh: 如果要你预测会以什么方式破裂，最初的裂痕迹象是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think usually the first sign comes with some major debt default.
zh: 我认为通常第一个迹象来自某次重大的债务违约。

speaker: Unknown
en: Generally, equity is never the reason why these things crack because equity, you write it down, you just take the loss.
zh: 一般来说，股权从来不是这些东西破裂的原因，因为股权，你把它减记，你只是承受损失。

speaker: Unknown
en: Debt, on the other hand, people have this expectation they're going to get paid back.
zh: 而债务则不同，人们抱着会被偿还的预期。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so most of the cycles I know, it breaks because people lever themselves.
zh: 所以我所知的大多数周期，破裂都是因为人们给自己加了杠杆。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you see what happened with Leopold, an incredible investor, right.
zh: 所以如果你看看 Leopold 身上发生的事，他是一位了不起的投资者，对吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you're 4X leverage, it doesn't matter if you're right.
zh: 但当你有 4 倍杠杆时，你正确与否并不重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to also get the timing correct.
zh: 你还得把时机也弄对。

speaker: Unknown
en: Missed his risk management class at high school, didn't he?
zh: 高中时没上风险管理课，是吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Poor old Leopold, when the music's going.
zh: 可怜的老 Leopold，趁着音乐还在响的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yes, I completely get you there.
zh: 所以是的，在这一点上我完全理解你。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you feel about the multiple tranche rounds so quickly?
zh: 你怎么看如此快速的多次分层融资（tranche rounds）？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm meeting founders very often where they're like, oh, we're doing a round this week at 100, but then we'll be opening up the second turn of it later next week at 200 because we've got so much demand.
zh: 我经常见到创始人说：哦，我们这周在 100 的估值融资，但下周晚些时候我们会开放第二档，在 200 的估值，因为需求太大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: This just gives me shivers and I feel like we buy any gold or we buy any car.
zh: 这让我脊背发凉，感觉就像“我们买任何黄金”或“我们买任何车”。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like in every cycle, you get the innovators, then you get the imitators, and then you eventually get the idiots.
zh: 我感觉每个周期里，先出现创新者，然后出现模仿者，最后出现蠢货。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the innovation of the tranche financing was the notion that I can get build with me money, and then use that build with me money at a lower valuation to get just money at higher valuation, and then eventually transition to just pure dumb money.
zh: 我认为分层融资的创新在于这样一种想法：我可以先拿“和我一起建设”的钱，然后用这笔“和我一起建设”的钱在较低估值去拿到“只是钱”的钱（在更高估值），最后过渡到纯粹的蠢钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's the logic of this, right?
zh: 我认为这就是这套逻辑，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I don't need like money.
zh: 所以我并不只是随便要钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: All money is not the same.
zh: 所有的钱并不都是一样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I will bring in some investors who are going to actually build a company with me, and then I will bring in some capital along, and then eventually I'll bring in some very low cost of capital.
zh: 我会引入一些真正会和我一起打造公司的投资者，然后再引入一些顺带跟投的资本，最后引入一些成本非常低的资本。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was the intention.
zh: 这才是本意。

speaker: Unknown
en: But again, like everything else, now people, everyone's doing it.
zh: 但话说回来,就像所有其他事情一样,现在人人都在这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not tied to the quality of the company anymore.
zh: 而且它不再和公司的质量挂钩了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's become another technique for people to do.
zh: 它变成了人们使用的又一种技巧。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I find like these things start initially with some, the core of the idea is actually a good one.
zh: 所以我发现这类事情起初都有一些——这个想法的核心其实是好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, I want to actually raise capital, but I want to distinguish between capital that adds value and capital that doesn't add value.
zh: 好的,我确实想要融资,但我想区分能带来价值的资本和不带来价值的资本。

speaker: Unknown
en: Will you do it as a firm if you'll come in in the latter tranche?
zh: 如果你是在后面的批次进来,你们公司会做吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely depends on the situation.
zh: 完全取决于情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have been on both sides of this situation, and I think if the company is interesting, the founders are special, absolutely.
zh: 我们在这件事的两边都经历过,我认为如果这家公司有意思、创始人很特别,那绝对可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really?
zh: 真的吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the end of the day, I never care about what other people invest, what they do.
zh: 说到底,我从来不在乎别人投什么、做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm looking at this round and say- Are you not hurt by the fact that they are saying you're legitimately less valuable than Peter Fenton, who we're letting in at half the price?
zh: 我看的是这一轮,然后说——他们说你合理地比 Peter Fenton 价值更低,而我们让他以半价进来,你难道不为此受伤吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Peter is amazing.
zh: Peter 很了不起。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the biggest thing I've learned over time is you never want to let your ego come in the way.
zh: 我认为我随时间学到的最重要的一件事就是,你永远不要让自我(ego)挡在中间。

speaker: Unknown
en: My only ego is to make money for my investors.
zh: 我唯一的自我就是为我的投资人赚钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I can make money for my investors, who the hell cares?
zh: 如果我能为我的投资人赚钱,谁他妈在乎呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: Have you let your ego ever get in the way?
zh: 你的自我有没有曾经挡过路?

speaker: Unknown
en: I have done.
zh: 我有过。

speaker: Unknown
zh: 百分之百有过。

speaker: Unknown
en: What happened?
zh: 发生了什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you get caught in ways of around negotiating for valuation or being in a syndicate, or sometimes you're offered the opportunity where you think you're offered a small piece and you're like, well, I'm too big for that piece.
zh: 我认为你会陷入各种情形,比如围绕估值谈判,或者加入联合投资(syndicate),或者有时你得到一个机会,你以为别人只给你一小块,你就想,哼,我太大了,不适合那一小块。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in this business, you have to have a high degree of humility because
zh: 我认为在这一行,你必须有高度的谦逊,因为

speaker: Unknown
en: Every week I get hit, I get punched in my face by things I don't know.
zh: 每周我都会被我不知道的东西击中,被打在脸上。

speaker: Unknown
en: The biggest mistakes are when we get too caught in our ego.
zh: 最大的错误都出现在我们太被自我困住的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, the reality is simple.
zh: 你看,现实很简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: We raise money from institutional investors with one and one new goal, which is to return more of them back.
zh: 我们从机构投资人那里募资,只有一个目标,就是把更多钱还给他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: If there's an opportunity to make money on investment, we should do it.
zh: 如果有在一个投资上赚钱的机会,我们就应该做。

speaker: Unknown
en: The rest of this is all noise.
zh: 其余的一切都是噪音。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think too often, because venture capital tends to be dominated by personalities, people get caught in this.
zh: 而且我认为,因为风险投资往往由个性人物主导,人们太容易陷入其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: You probably don't know a lot of people at Goldman.
zh: 你可能不认识高盛的很多人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody can say David Solomon, who's a CEO.
zh: 但人人都能说出 CEO David Solomon 的名字。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the idea is Goldman makes a ton of money, and those people just go and do their job.
zh: 但重点是,高盛赚很多钱,而那些人只是去做好自己的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Too often, venture capital, we end up, because there's so many personalities and people, it becomes more about who and our ego as opposed to just do the job.
zh: 太常见的是,风险投资因为有这么多个性和人物,最终变成更多是关于谁以及我们的自我,而不是只把工作做好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's forced by the fact that we are fighting for constrained supply, though.
zh: 但我认为这是被一个事实逼出来的,就是我们在争夺受限的供给。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're looking at, say, Goldman's public team, you can buy NVIDIA, I can buy NVIDIA, they can buy NVIDIA.
zh: 如果你看,比如说,高盛的公募团队,你可以买 NVIDIA,我可以买 NVIDIA,他们也可以买 NVIDIA。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is a free market.
zh: 这是一个自由市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here, we are both competing for Max at Lagora, and our check, if he takes yours, he won't take mine, because there's one lead check.
zh: 而在这里,我们俩都在争夺 Lagora 的 Max,而我们的支票,如果他拿了你的,就不会拿我的,因为只有一张领投支票。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we have to have personality, we have to sell ourselves, because there is a constrained supply, no?
zh: 所以我们必须有个性,我们必须推销自己,因为供给是受限的,不是吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What you say is absolutely true, which is that you have to have these two dualities and manage them.
zh: 你说的绝对正确,就是你必须拥有这两种双重性并管理好它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is you have to have a personality.
zh: 一个是你必须有个性。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to be able to project a sense of differentiation, right?
zh: 你必须能够展现出一种差异化感,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because why does someone choose Harry and not me?
zh: 因为为什么有人选 Harry 而不选我?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's because they like Harry.
zh: 是因为他们喜欢 Harry。

speaker: Unknown
en: And good looks and charm.
zh: 还有好外表和魅力。

speaker: Unknown
en: I see that in person, even more so.
zh: 见到真人后,我更加体会到这一点了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think if you get caught in that and you get so immersed in it, then you lose the sense of what the core purpose is, right?
zh: 但我认为,如果你陷在里面,陷得太深,那你就失去了对核心目标的把握,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: The core purpose of having that personality and charm is to make money for your investors.
zh: 拥有那种个性和魅力的核心目标,是为你的投资人赚钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why it is, right?
zh: 这就是目的所在,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And if there's a time for you to make money for your investors where you have to let your ego take a backseat, you should do it, and that's the right thing to do.
zh: 而如果有那么一个时刻,你要为投资人赚钱而必须让自我退居其次,你就应该这么做,那才是正确的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, I'm not saying it's easy to do.
zh: 现在，我并不是说这很容易做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not saying I've done it, but it's the right thing to do.
zh: 我不是说我做到了，但这是该做的正确的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's kind of like, I know I gotta eat, ride, and exercise.
zh: 这有点像，我知道我得好好吃饭、骑车、锻炼。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know that.
zh: 我知道这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't do it often, but I know it's the right thing to do.
zh: 我不常做到，但我知道那是该做的正确的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, but Jim Khan is so good.
zh: 是啊，但 Jim Khan 实在太厉害了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some things in life are worth it, like butter chicken.
zh: 生活中有些事是值得的，比如黄油鸡。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm a dashum.
zh: 我是达 SIMD教徒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, you are?
zh: 哦，是吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, well done.
zh: 哦，那不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, don't worry.
zh: 嗯，别担心。

speaker: Unknown
en: I like a dashum, too.
zh: 我也喜欢达 SIMD。

speaker: Unknown
en: We said about price, kind of, hey, we're a little bit less focused on it when it's early.
zh: 我们说过价格的事，可以说，嗯，在早期我们相对不那么关注它。

speaker: Unknown
en: There comes a time when it does matter, with the greatest of respects.
zh: 但总会有那么一个时刻，它确实重要，恕我直言。

speaker: Unknown
en: Say it.
zh: 说出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Say it.
zh: 说出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Men are kind of pay up.
zh: 男人们就是会出高价。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for all you entrepreneurs out there, we definitely pay up.
zh: 还有各位创业者，我们绝对会出高价。

speaker: Unknown
en: So definitely call us.
zh: 所以一定要联系我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, you do.
zh: 是的，你们会的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And every time I'm like, pfff, men are paying up.
zh: 每次我都会想，啧，男人们就是会出高价。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you prove me right.
zh: 而你们一次次证明我是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, you're right.
zh: 就像，你说得对。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm proved wrong when I'm like, God, they're not disciplined on price.
zh: 而当我想“天哪，他们在价格上真没纪律”时，我就被证明是错的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I guess I'm questioning, do we just need to completely reshape how we think about terms and market sizing?
zh: 所以我在想，我们是不是需要彻底重塑我们对条款和市场规模测算的思考方式？

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's think about when people pay up.
zh: 让我们想想人们什么时候会出高价。

speaker: Unknown
en: People just sometimes pay up to be able to win the deal.
zh: 有时人们出高价就是为了赢得这轮融资。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think sometimes people pay up because they're able to see a bigger TAM than the other investor.
zh: 我认为有时人们出高价是因为他们能比其他投资人看到更大的 TAM。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in those cases, you're not actually paying a higher market price.
zh: 在那些情况下，你实际上并没有支付更高的市场价格。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're able to see that the opportunity is bigger, and therefore you're willing to see that possibility.
zh: 你是能看到这个机会更大，因此你愿意看到那种可能性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, sometimes you're going to be right.
zh: 当然，有时你会是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes you're going to be wrong.
zh: 有时你会是错的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So to me, I don't necessarily think it's just price.
zh: 所以对我而言，我不认为这仅仅只是价格问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes you don't see the TAM.
zh: 有时你看不到 TAM。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're just trying to win the deal, and that's what the price it takes.
zh: 你只是想赢下这轮融资，这就是需要付出的价格。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're just a clear price taker.
zh: 你就是一个彻底的价格接受者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that happens too.
zh: 这种情况也会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem is venture is an asymmetric game.
zh: 问题是，风投是一场不对称的游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can lose the dollars you invest, but you can make 10x if you're right.
zh: 你可能损失你投资的钱，但如果看对了你能赚 10 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that asymmetry means that the sense of omissions are way higher than the sense of commissions.
zh: 这种不对称意味着遗漏错误带来的损失远高于佣金错误带来的损失。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I mean by that is you only see the deals we do, right?
zh: 我的意思是，你只看到我们做了的交易，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't see the deals we pass.
zh: 你看不到我们放过的交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the most expensive mistakes venture capitalists make are the deals they passed, not the deals they did.
zh: 但风投投资人犯的最昂贵的错误，是他们放过的交易，而不是他们做的交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you say that, what's the most memorable past that haunts you?
zh: 你这么说的话，哪一次放过最让你难忘、最折磨你？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is it?
zh: 是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: My most memorable past was that I was a young board member on a company called Plaxo, which had an incredible board.
zh: 我最难忘的一次放过，是我在一家叫 Plaxo 的公司担任年轻的董事会成员，那家公司有一个非常厉害的董事会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mike Moritz, Ram Sriram, Tim Kugel from Yahoo, and Little Unknown Me, and Sean Parker, and Todd Masonis, and was the founder, and Cameron Wren.
zh: Mike Moritz、Ram Sriram、来自 Yahoo 的 Tim Kugel，还有默默无闻的我，还有 Sean Parker，还有 Todd Masonis，他是创始人，还有 Cameron Wren。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sean had some challenges on that board and was asked to leave that board.
zh: Sean 在那个董事会上遇到了一些麻烦，被要求离开董事会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I was the only person within 10 years of his age in that group.
zh: 因为我是那群人里唯一和他年龄相差在 10 岁以内的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was telling me he was going to Boston and he's going to work with his college dropout.
zh: 他告诉我说他要去波士顿，和他大学时期辍学的伙伴一起干活。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's like, you should get involved.
zh: 然后他说,你应该参与进去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, Sean, you just got booted out of this sport.
zh: 我就说,Sean,你刚被这个行业踢出来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I have no idea what I'm doing.
zh: 而且我完全不知道自己在干什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I didn't even take that meeting.
zh: 结果我连那次会都没去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I probably had the opportunity to write a $50,000 check.
zh: 我很可能错失了写一张五万美元支票的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And those seed rounds were different.
zh: 那时候的种子轮不一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were million-dollar seed rounds.
zh: 那是一百万美元的种子轮。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a tough one.
zh: 这可真让人难受。

speaker: Unknown
en: What was Sean like back then?
zh: 那时候的Sean是什么样的人?

speaker: Unknown
en: The way he described Plaxel, his vision worked out.
zh: 他描述Plaxel的方式,他的愿景成真了。

speaker: Unknown
en: He understood virality, network effects, his thought process around what happened at Napster.
zh: 他懂病毒式传播、网络效应,他对Napster发生的事情的思考过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: So my rule of thumb is I'm always looking for people who are incredibly good at communicating very complex concepts in a simple manner and just have insight.
zh: 所以我的经验法则是,我总是在寻找那些极其擅长用简单的方式传达非常复杂的概念、并且有洞察力的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Sean just had insight around human behavior and complex concepts and could boil it down in a simple way.
zh: 而Sean对人类行为和复杂概念就是有洞察力,并且能用简单的方式把它讲透。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was a very good communicator.
zh: 他是一个非常好的沟通者。

speaker: Unknown
en: What a character.
zh: 真是个角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: He gets to have Justin Timberlake play him.
zh: 他还让Justin Timberlake来演他。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's a pretty cool one.
zh: 我是说,这挺酷的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Drop the the.
zh: 把the去掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Love it.
zh: 我认为这些东西都有点像《少数派报告》。

speaker: Unknown
en: We actually did that.
zh: 我们其实真的这么做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were at the 20-minute VC, now it's just 20-minute VC.
zh: 我们原来是the 20-minute VC,现在就叫20-minute VC了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, there you go.
zh: 哦,这就对了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
zh: 是啊,是啊,是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks, dude.
zh: 谢了,哥们。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was talking to Amy beforehand, speaking of kind of the founders you back there.
zh: 我之前在和Amy聊,说到你投资的那些创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Amazing partner of mine.
zh: 她是我非常棒的合伙人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Amazing partner of yours.
zh: 也是你非常棒的合伙人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And she said that you care a lot about understanding what brought founders together.
zh: 她说你很在意了解是什么让创始人走到一起的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hearing about your talking about Sean there made me think of this.
zh: 听你刚才聊Sean让我想到了这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why do you care about what brings founders together?
zh: 你为什么在意是什么把创始人凝聚到一起的?

speaker: Unknown
en: And are there any patterns or signals that excite you?
zh: 有没有什么让你兴奋的模式或信号?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the company you build is a team you build.
zh: 我认为你建立的公司就是你建立的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, so much of the DNA of a company is set by its founding team.
zh: 一家公司的DNA很大程度上是由它的创始团队设定的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what brought them together?
zh: 所以是什么把他们聚到一起的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Why they thought in a world of six billion people, they should be the people to do this?
zh: 为什么他们觉得在六十亿人的世界里,应该由他们来做这件事?

speaker: Unknown
en: How they think about each of the strengths and weaknesses?
zh: 他们如何看待彼此的优势和劣势?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think these things all sort of like minority report.
zh: 我觉得这些事情都有点像《少数派报告》(minority report)。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're like a precog that tells you around how they're going to make decisions, how they're going to build the rest of their team.
zh: 它们就像一个预知者,告诉你他们将会如何做决策、如何组建他们剩下的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think it gives you a clue about who are these people.
zh: 所以我认为这能给你一个线索,知道这些人是谁。

speaker: Unknown
en: And ultimately, I think the company's culture and DNA are going to be shaped by the founders.
zh: 归根结底,我认为公司的文化和DNA将由创始人塑造。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can ask one question that you find most revealing of a founder quality.
zh: 你可以问一个你认为最能揭示创始人特质的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Doug Leone is to me, it was the one I remember most.
zh: 对我来说,Doug Leone的那个问题是我印象最深的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he always says, what's your worst reference?
zh: 他总是问:你最差的推荐人是谁?

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, that's a great question.
zh: 你知道,这是个很棒的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I generally ask your five best friends, right?
zh: 我一般会问,你最要好的五个朋友,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And imagine they're in a room, and if I had to ask them three words to describe you, what would that be?
zh: 想象他们在一个房间里,如果我要用三个词来形容你,那会是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a question I normally ask people.
zh: 这是我通常问别人的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll tell you, I listened to Mike Moritz on the interview, and he asked a question, and his favorite question is, if you could go back in your life and change one thing, what would that be?
zh: 跟你说,我听了Mike Moritz的那期访谈,他问了一个问题,他最喜欢的问题是:如果你能回到过去,改变生活中的一件事,那会是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's a pretty interesting question.
zh: 我觉得这是个挺有意思的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I were to ask you what you think about yourself, it's harder, but when you think about your friends, you can sort of externalize it, and then that gives you a clue about how the people around you think about you, and it also tells you your self-awareness.
zh: 如果我问你如何看待自己,这会更难,但当你想到你的朋友时,你可以某种程度上把它外化,这能给你一个线索,知道你周围的人怎么看你,同时也能看出你的自我认知。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because usually after I do that, I also do references and I'm trying to see if the references match someone's self-awareness, right?
zh: 因为通常在我做完那件事之后,我还会做背景调查(reference),我想看看背景调查是否与某个人的自我认知相符,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually okay if you know your weaknesses, then you have a much better chance of managing them.
zh: 其实,如果你了解自己的弱点,那也没关系,那你管理它们的机会就大得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the people who are blind to their weaknesses that usually have challenges.
zh: 通常有麻烦的,是那些对自己的弱点视而不见的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't mind, my weaknesses are revealed in the comments section of every interview, so I see them glaringly.
zh: 别介意,我的弱点在每一次访谈的评论区里都会被揭露,所以我看得一清二楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: One thing that's been uniform across the industry is we've seen ownerships go down.
zh: 整个行业里有一件事是一致的:我们观察到 ownership(持股比例)在下降。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even the hailed benchmark now take less than 10%.
zh: 即使是现在备受推崇的 benchmark(标杆案例),持股也不到 10%。

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought they said 20% are bust.
zh: 我记得他们说过 20% 的都破了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe let's stick to that message.
zh: 也许我们就维持这个说法吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love the benchmark, guys.
zh: 我很喜欢这个 benchmark,各位。

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely.
zh: 完全同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: But does ownership matter as much anymore?
zh: 但 ownership 现在还那么重要吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course it does.
zh: 当然重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ownership always matters, but I think you have to think of that relative to the opportunity, right?
zh: Ownership 永远重要,但我认为你必须把它相对于机会来考虑,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: What I mean by that is, yeah, would I love to have 20% of a company?
zh: 我的意思是,是的,我难道不想拥有一家公司 20% 的股份吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Sure.
zh: 当然想。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I'd rather take 2% of a trillion dollar company than 20% of a hundred million dollar company, right?
zh: 但我宁愿要一家万亿美元公司 2% 的股份,也不要一家一亿美元公司 20% 的股份,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So you'll do deals now for 2%, 3%?
zh: 那你们现在会做 2%、3% 的交易?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, we did.
zh: 嗯,我们做过。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anthropic, we own less than 2%.
zh: Anthropic,我们持有的股份不到 2%。

speaker: Unknown
en: My point is that I think when you think about ownership, you can't think of that in isolation.
zh: 我的观点是,当你考虑 ownership 时,不能孤立地考虑它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think you're either in the ownership game or you're in the money movement game.
zh: 但我认为,你要么玩的是 ownership 的游戏,要么玩的是资金规模游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: I disagree a little bit.
zh: 我有一点不同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think when you're getting your option bet, you want to have ownership because when it's not clear, so let's say you know it's an outlier.
zh: 我认为当你下你的期权注时,你会想要拥有 ownership,因为当情况还不明朗时——假设你知道它是一个异类(outlier)。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's an outlier company, then you are in the capital invested game.
zh: 如果它是一家异类公司,那你就是在投入资本的game里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Prior to being an outlier company, you have to be in the ownership game.
zh: 而在它成为异类公司之前,你必须处在 ownership 的游戏里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your best situation is you're in the ownership game in an outlier company, and then you go into the money movement game.
zh: 你最好的处境是,你在一家异类公司里拥有 ownership,然后再进入资金规模游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, I thought the ownership doesn't matter pre it being an outlier because you're there for the information.
zh: 不,我以为在它成为异类之前 ownership 并不重要,因为你在那里是为了信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: When it does become known, it becomes a money concentration game.
zh: 当它变得广为人知时,它就变成了资金集中游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want to have enough ownership, though.
zh: 不过你还是要拥有足够的 ownership。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you look at Hicksfield.
zh: 我是说,你看看 Hicksfield。

speaker: Unknown
en: My partner, Amy, she killed it.
zh: 我的合伙人 Amy,她干得漂亮极了。

speaker: Unknown
en: She got 15% of the company for a $5 million check.
zh: 她用一张 500 万美元的支票拿到了公司 15% 的股份。

speaker: Unknown
en: You had Alex on your podcast.
zh: 你上过 Alex 的播客——

speaker: Unknown
en: Incredible entrepreneur, incredible business.
zh: 非常了不起的创业者,非常了不起的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in that case, we got the ownership.
zh: 所以在那个案例里,我们拿到了 ownership。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we also have the opportunity to then size up.
zh: 然后我们还有机会随后加仓扩大仓位。

speaker: Unknown
en: Did you?
zh: 你们加了吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, we've invested.
zh: 是的,我们投资了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you get my rationale, though, for actually it doesn't matter if you have ownership in the first place.
zh: 但你理解我的逻辑吗?也就是说,一开始有没有 ownership 其实并不重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: What you're buying is the information to size up.
zh: 你买到的是用来加仓的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: I get that.
zh: 我明白。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're asking me, is it better to be in the company regardless of ownership or not be in the company?
zh: 如果你问我,是不管有没有 ownership 都在那家公司里更好,还是不在那家公司里?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it's better to be in the company.
zh: 是的,在那家公司里更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's even better to be in the company with ownership because now you actually have gotten your ownership that's going to drive real returns.
zh: 但是,带着 ownership 在那家公司里还要更好,因为这时你实际上已经拿到了将驱动真实回报的 ownership。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because the problem is, once there's an outlier, everybody knows about it.
zh: 因为问题是,一旦出现异类,所有人都知道了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's no longer a selection game.
zh: 它不再是一场筛选游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just, okay, can you get access?
zh: 只剩:好吧,你能不能拿到额度?

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's a position sizing game.
zh: 而且这是一场仓位规模游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no alpha there.
zh: 那里没有 alpha。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's true.
zh: 这话没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the AI greatest hits, everybody knows these companies.
zh: 在 AI 的金曲榜单里,人人都知道这些公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: How much of your fund will you put in a single company?
zh: 你的基金会有多少比例投给单一一家公司?

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think we would put more than 20% of it.
zh: 我认为我们不会投超过 20%。

speaker: Unknown
en: Have you gone up to 20% before?
zh: 你以前有到过 20% 吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: We have hit 20% on one company.
zh: 我们在一家公司上达到过 20%。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whoa.
zh: 作为一家离群值公司,你能有多大的信念?

speaker: Unknown
en: What company?
zh: 哪家公司?

speaker: Unknown
en: Anthropic.
zh: Anthropic。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's gotta be an exception, right?
zh: 这肯定得是个例外,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: But that was a hard conversation.
zh: 但那是一场很艰难的谈话。

speaker: Unknown
en: We 10X this year, we 10X last year.
zh: 我们今年涨了 10 倍,去年也涨了 10 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, thank you, let's do it.
zh: 好吧,谢谢你,那就干吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I do feel that you have to think about the question of ownership and concentration as when.
zh: 但我确实觉得,你必须把持股比例和集中度的问题当作「何时」来思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I mean is that where was the company?
zh: 我的意思是,这家公司当时处在什么位置?

speaker: Unknown
en: What information do you have?
zh: 你掌握什么信息?

speaker: Unknown
en: How much conviction can you have as an outlier company?
zh: 作为一家特立独行的公司，你能有多少信念？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because the thing about position sizing is you want to position sizes when the data is there.
zh: 因为仓位管理的关键在于,你要在数据出现时才加仓。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you position size it ahead of the data, then you're taking a lot more risk.
zh: 如果你在数据出现之前就加仓,那你承担的风险就大得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the question is not, did you put 20% of the fund of the company in one check at the beginning of the fund, or did you ladder up to 20% on the basis of new data?
zh: 所以问题不是,你在基金一开始就一次性把基金的 20% 投给一家公司,还是你基于新数据逐步加仓到 20%?

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, it's much better to ladder up on the basis of new data.
zh: 显然,基于新数据逐步加仓要好得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think in an era where venture capitalists are going to have ownership come down, right?
zh: 而且我认为,在一个风险投资人的持股比例将会下降的时代,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I wish we could get 10%.
zh: 我是说,我真希望能拿到 10%。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even 10% is hard, right?
zh: 就连 10% 都很难,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Now your way you're going to win is you're going to establish a position and then size up as a company does well so that you have sized it, commensurate to the outlier opportunity.
zh: 现在你的赢法是,先建立仓位,然后随着公司表现好而加大仓位,这样你的仓位规模才能与离群值机会相称。

speaker: Unknown
en: Totally get you and get that.
zh: 完全理解你,也理解这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And everyone says, but ownership doesn't matter so much because outcome sizes are so much larger than they've ever been.
zh: 而且每个人都说,持股比例没那么重要,因为结果的规模比以往任何时候都大得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they are.
zh: 确实如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is a valid answer.
zh: 这是个有效的回答。

speaker: Unknown
en: My question is, are they on the whole?
zh: 我的问题是,整体上它们真的更大了吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, do we just have a breadth of companies that will be much larger?
zh: 就是说,我们是不是会有一批规模大得多的公司?

speaker: Unknown
en: Or is it really just a handful of Anthropics and SpaceX?
zh: 还是说其实只有少数几家 Anthropic 和 SpaceX?

speaker: Unknown
en: And Cursor on the small land at 60 billion, which is still enormous and amazing.
zh: 还有 Cursor 在小额阶段达到 600 亿,这仍然巨大且惊人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But is that a good enough justification for ownerships going down?
zh: 但这足以成为持股比例下降的正当理由吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the problem comes down to your portfolio composition, right?
zh: 我认为问题归结于你的投资组合构成,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: If you are in one of those outliers, I think you can survive with low ownership.
zh: 如果你在那些离群值之一里面,我认为你可以靠低持股比例活下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what happens if you are not in these big outliers?
zh: 但如果你不在这些大的离群值里面,会怎么样?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because essentially, you're playing a game, to use baseball analogies, you're playing a game where there's only Grand Slam home runs or strikeouts.
zh: 因为本质上,用棒球来打比方,你玩的是一个只有全垒打或三振出局的比赛。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no singles, doubles, or triples, right?
zh: 没有一垒安打、二垒安打或三垒安打,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And in cricket terms, it's only scoring sixes and not having ones and twos.
zh: 用板球来说,就是只能得六分,没有一分和两分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the problem with that is that if you don't score the six and you don't have the ones and twos, that's going to be a tough fund.
zh: 问题在于,如果你没打出六分,又没有一分和两分,那这个基金就很难熬了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so part of getting ownership is giving some insurance for you that if you missed out on the outlier, the sort of midsize outcomes can still move the needle for you.
zh: 所以拿到持股比例的一部分意义,就是给你一点保险,如果你错过了那个离群值,那些中型规模的结果仍然能对你的基金产生实质影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: But will you do singles and doubles?
zh: 但你会去打一垒和二垒安打吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: No, the goal is always to score home runs, right?
zh: 不会,目标永远是打出全垒打,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: But sometimes you strike out.
zh: 但有时候你会三振出局。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you strike out all the time, that's going to be a tough fund.
zh: 所以如果你总是三振出局,那这个基金就很难熬了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the idea is that you want to at least say, okay, I went for the home run and I got a triple.
zh: 所以这个想法是,你至少可以说,好吧,我去追全垒打,结果打出了三垒安打。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I just don't think founders are aware, and I say this, and people always get at me, and I think they kind of miss the point, because I say it lovingly for awareness of founders that the game has changed and that, you know, going from one to four million,
zh: 但我只是不认为创始人意识到这一点,我说这个,人们总是来怼我,我觉得他们有点没抓住重点,因为我是出于对创始人的关怀、出于让你们知情才说的:游戏已经变了,你知道的,从一百万到四百万,

speaker: Unknown
en: And then four to eight million and then eight to 16.
zh: 然后四百万到八百万,再从八百万到一千六百万。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then banking in five years time, we're going to hit 30.
zh: 然后指望五年后,我们会达到三千万。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's an amazing achievement, but it is just not enough to get venture excited today.
zh: 那是很了不起的成就,但放在今天,这根本不足以让风险投资兴奋起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you agree with that?
zh: 你同意这个看法吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, I agree with that.
zh: 是的,我同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, snapshot in time because you're seeing companies.
zh: 再说一次,这只是某个时间点的快照,因为你看到的是这些公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: But do you think venture will ever go back to being excited about that?
zh: 但你觉得风投有一天会重新对那种东西感到兴奋吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, they're not excited about it today because they're seeing companies go from 1 to 10 to 50 to 100.
zh: 嗯,他们今天对它不兴奋,是因为他们看到公司从 1 涨到 10、到 50、再到 100。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they're getting to 100 in three years.
zh: 所以他们三年就做到 100。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in some cases, they're going from zero to 1 billion in 18 months, right?
zh: 所以在某些情况下,他们 18 个月就从零做到 10 亿,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So when you see those kind of companies, of course you want to do those.
zh: 所以当你看到那种公司时,你当然想做那些。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's because we are a moment in time where there's certain trends allowing you to do it.
zh: 但那是因为我们正处在这样一个时刻,有某些趋势让你能够做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think this continues forever.
zh: 我不认为这会永远持续下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think this is where I think you have to take the long, long horizon look at this, right?
zh: 所以我认为这正是你必须用非常、非常长的视角来看待它的地方,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: There were companies who grow fast, but there's a combination of things that make these companies grow fast today that may or may not continue.
zh: 曾经有增长很快的公司,但今天是多种因素结合让这些公司增长这么快,而这些因素可能会也可能不会持续。

speaker: Unknown
en: When they grow as fast as they are, the rounds come thick and fast, and the prices are high.
zh: 当它们以现在这种速度增长时,融资轮次来得又密又快,而且估值很高。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you look at instinct.
zh: 我是说,你看看 instinct。

speaker: Unknown
en: God bless.
zh: 愿上帝保佑。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wish they've gone from, I don't know, 250 million to 10 billion in 10 weeks.
zh: 我真希望他们已经从,我不确定,2.5 亿在 10 周内涨到了 100 亿。

speaker: Unknown
en: Would you have done that round at 10 billion?
zh: 你会在 100 亿的估值参与那一轮吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Smart people have done it.
zh: 聪明人已经这么做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are in town, which we love, and we think very highly of, and we're excited about that.
zh: 我们投资了 town,我们很喜欢它,对它评价很高,而且我们对此感到兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that there's something going on there.
zh: 我觉得那边有事情正在发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a true phenomenon.
zh: 那是一个真实的现象。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I don't know is to understand their data and what it costs for them to keep growing their user base.
zh: 我不知道的是,要理解他们的数据,以及他们继续扩大用户群的成本是多少。

speaker: Unknown
en: And how does the Muse launch affect their growth?
zh: 还有 Muse 的发布会如何影响他们的增长?

speaker: Unknown
en: Can I ask you, everyone kind of goes into a lot of investing now with the idea that there's downside protection.
zh: 我能问一下吗,现在大家做投资时都带着一种有下行保护的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Noah's incredible.
zh: Noah 非常了不起。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's in a very strategic space for the incumbents.
zh: 它处在对现有巨头来说非常有战略意义的空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Worst case, one and a half billion LikPraf.
zh: 最坏的情况,15 亿,LikePraf。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a no brainer for Microsoft to do it as an addendum to Copilot or Apple to do it.
zh: 对微软来说,把它作为 Copilot 的附加部分收购是个不假思索的事,或者苹果来做也一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jesus, Apple, please do it.
zh: 天哪,苹果,求你做吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do us all a favor and save us from Siri.
zh: 帮我们大家一个忙,把我们从 Siri 手里解救出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think that downside protection, ah, don't worry, the incumbents will buy it, is okay to have or quite a dangerous mindset to have?
zh: 你觉得这种下行保护——"啊,别担心,现有巨头会收购它"——的想法是可以接受的,还是一种相当危险的心态?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you can easily rationalize a lot of things if you take that mindset.
zh: 我觉得如果你抱着那种心态,你很容易为很多事情找理由合理化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the problem is that, again, you threw out this billion and a half number, casually, because we are in this environment where, you know, AMD is buying a company for eight and a half billion, NVIDIA bought Hugging Face for 14 billion, you know, Stripe bought OpenRouter allegedly for an eight billion, you know.
zh: 而问题在于,再说一次,你随口抛出了这个 15 亿的数字,因为我们正处在这样的环境里,你知道的,AMD 正在以 85 亿收购一家公司,NVIDIA 以 140 亿收购了 Hugging Face,你知道,Stripe 据称以 80 亿收购了 OpenRouter,你知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Allegedly.
zh: 据称。

speaker: Unknown
en: Allegedly.
zh: 据称。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we have to go and say, these are points in time where companies are doing it.
zh: 而且我觉得我们必须去说,这些是公司正在做这类事情的时间点。

speaker: Unknown
en: It may not be that way.
zh: 情况可能不会一直是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so today, it feels like a billion and a half is, oh, no big deal.
zh: 所以今天,15 亿感觉像是,"哦,没什么大不了。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I'm right, it's going to be worth 100, 200 billion.
zh: 如果我是对的,它会值 1000 亿、2000 亿。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I'm wrong, someone is going to pick it up for 3, 4 billion.
zh: 如果我错了,有人会以 30 亿、40 亿把它捡走。"

speaker: Unknown
en: By the way, that's what you're referring to my tweets.
zh: 顺便说一下,你说的就是我那些推文。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wrote this thing about if you go back and look at doing the dot-com era, Nortel bought Kairos for $3.5 billion.
zh: 我写过一篇东西,如果你回溯看互联网泡沫时代,Nortel 以 35 亿收购了 Kairos。

speaker: Unknown
en: Lucent bought Chromatis for $4.5 billion.
zh: Lucent 以 45 亿收购了 Chromatis。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are companies with no product, no revenue, just teams, and they bought it with their stock, and so it felt very similar.
zh: 这些公司没有产品、没有收入,只有团队,而且它们是用自己的股票来收购的,所以感觉非常相似。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, I believe Jeff Yang from Redpoint, legendary investor,
zh: 事实上,我相信 Redpoint 的 Jeff Yang,传奇投资人,

speaker: Unknown
en: had this code in the internet standard, which is a magazine that doesn't exist anymore.
zh: 在互联网标准(The Internet Standard)——那本已经不存在的杂志上——有过这句名言。

speaker: Unknown
en: He said, you know, there's no risk in venture capital.
zh: 他说,你知道,风险投资没有风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: If the company is successful, it'll be sold for billions.
zh: 如果公司成功,它会以数十亿被卖掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: If not, it'll be bought for the Perp stack.
zh: 如果不成功,它会以 Perp stack 的价格被买走。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it didn't quite work out that way on the other end of the cycle after March 2000.
zh: 而在 2000 年 3 月之后，周期的另一端并没有完全按那样发展。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I go with trepidation, but I just wouldn't take the mindset, oh, some large strategy is going to buy my company for the provincial stack, because they don't care about the investors.
zh: 所以我是怀着忐忑去的，但我就是不会抱着这种心态——哦，某个大型战略方会因为那点微不足道的技术栈来收购我的公司，因为他们并不在乎投资人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They care about the founders.
zh: 他们在乎的是创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why would they do that?
zh: 他们为什么要那么做？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why wouldn't they just hire the founders for the same package?
zh: 为什么不直接用同样的待遇把创始人招过去呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: In a lot of cases, they kind of are in these structured deals, let's be honest, and screwing the investors.
zh: 说实话，在很多情况下，他们在这些结构化的交易里差不多就是这么干的，把投资人坑了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you've seen that, and you can't take that.
zh: 所以你见过这种情况，而你不能指望那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no reason for them to take care of the cap table.
zh: 他们没有任何理由去照顾股权结构表。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think about the dilutive nature of businesses today?
zh: 你有想过如今企业的稀释问题吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I mean by that is just like we are suffering more and more dilution as an investor class than ever before, and it's a better time than ever to be an employee given the levels of stock-based compensation, SBC for people.
zh: 我的意思是，作为投资人类别，我们正遭受着比以往任何时候都更严重的稀释，而鉴于股权激励水平，对员工来说是前所未有的好时代，也就是 SBC(股权激励)。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you worry about that?
zh: 你担心这个吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Think about that?
zh: 想过这个吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Should I worry about that and think about that?
zh: 我应该担心并思考这个问题吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: For sure.
zh: 当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we look at whatever we invest in at the seed round, and we assume by the time we sell or exit the company, if we own 10%, we would have 3.5% to 4%.
zh: 我是说，我们在种子轮投资任何项目时，都会假设到我们卖出或退出公司时，如果我们拥有 10%，那时只会剩 3.5% 到 4%。

speaker: Unknown
en: We expect 60% dilution from the point of our first check, right?
zh: 从我们开出第一张支票起，我们预期 60% 的稀释，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's a combination of dilution from financing, but it's a dilution from option pool expansions.
zh: 这是融资稀释的组合，但也来自期权池扩大的稀释。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you have to really think of yourself as whatever ownership you bought in your first check, it'll only be 50% by then at the end.
zh: 所以你必须真正把自己所买的股份理解为：你第一张支票买到的所有权，到最后只会剩 50%。

speaker: Unknown
en: The interesting thing is that it's very common in a lot of companies we're seeing today.
zh: 有意思的是，这在今天我们看到的很多公司里非常普遍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the other interesting thing is companies are sometimes scaling so fast, a la OpenRouter.
zh: 另一件有意思的事是，公司有时候扩张得非常快，比如 OpenRouter。

speaker: Unknown
en: Alex is a friend of both of ours, where they actually don't take that much dilution because they scale so fast, so quickly and so efficiently, where actually you suffer almost much less dilution.
zh: Alex 是我们俩共同的朋友，他们实际上没有承受那么多稀释，因为他们扩张得那么快、那么高效，实际上你遭受的稀释几乎少得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's almost a tale of two dilution worlds.
zh: 所以这几乎是一个稀释的两个世界的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you know what I mean?
zh: 你明白我的意思吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it's a function of time.
zh: 是的，这是时间的函数。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the way to think about it is that, and I don't think we spend enough time in venture capital thinking about it, we should say, what is the time horizon you're going to hold the company?
zh: 思考方式是——我不认为我们在风险投资行业花足够的时间思考这个——我们应该问：你打算持有这家公司的时间跨度是多长？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because the time horizon will determine your dilution.
zh: 因为时间跨度将决定你的稀释。

speaker: Unknown
en: So part of the reason when you are in situations where your dilution is less is they have quick exits.
zh: 所以当你处于稀释较少的情境时，部分原因是他们退出很快。

speaker: Unknown
en: They grew their value fastly, they have quick exits.
zh: 他们快速增长了价值，退出很快。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's a double win.
zh: 那是双重胜利。

speaker: Unknown
en: When your time horizon is long, there are two hits.
zh: 当你的时间跨度很长时，会有两次打击。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your IRA gets hit, and you're going to have meaningful dilution.
zh: 你的 IRR 会受到打击，而且你会承受显著的稀释。

speaker: Unknown
en: Did you think of that when investing, which is just like, what really is the ramp?
zh: 你投资的时候想过这个吗？就是说，真正的爬坡速度到底是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's businesses in the ERP space where they're like, ah, but the revenue is such high quality, Harry.
zh: ERP 领域有企业会说：啊，但收入质量很高啊，Harry。

speaker: Unknown
en: I get you, it's not as fast as your Higgsfield or your Lagora, but it's so high quality.
zh: 我理解你，它不像你的 Higgsfield 或 Lagora 那么快，但质量很高啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, yeah, fuck, it's slow.
zh: 然后我心想：对，妈的，就是慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Am I wrong to think that?
zh: 我这么想是错的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: No.
zh: 不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the velocity of the business is very important for venture capitalists, right?
zh: 我认为业务的速度对风险投资人来说非常重要，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And the velocity will determine a bunch of things, right?
zh: 而速度将决定很多事情，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because the other reason why your dilution goes down is if you have a fast uptick in valuation, the amount of ownership you've got to give for your next set of human capital is a lot lower, right?
zh: 因为你的稀释变少的另一个原因是，如果你的估值快速上升，你为下一批人力资本所需要让出的所有权比例就会低很多，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So you are a $200 million company and you're giving 2% of the company to hire a senior exec, right?
zh: 所以你是一家 2 亿美元的公司，你要给公司 2% 的股份去招一个高管，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's pretty meaningful.
zh: 那是相当可观的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You quickly become a $2 billion company.
zh: 而你很快变成一家 20 亿美元的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't need to get, you're going to give RSUs and you give the same person $20 million, which is 0.1%.
zh: 你不需要——你会给 RSU，你给同一个人 2000 万美元，也就是 0.1%。

speaker: Unknown
en: DPI or IRR?
zh: DPI 还是 IRR？

speaker: Unknown
en: Both.
zh: 都要。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you can.
zh: 我是说，你可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do think, actually, that you can't have IRR without DPI.
zh: 实际上我确实认为，没有 DPI 就不可能有 IRR。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the question you're trying to ask is, hey, will you settle for a larger DPI over longer horizon, or do you want quicker DPI with a faster IRR?
zh: 我想你想问的问题是：嘿，你是愿意接受更长周期下更大的 DPI，还是想要更快 IRR 下的更快的 DPI？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the reality of venture when I joined, this is now dating myself 28 years ago, people didn't focus on IRR.
zh: 我加入风投行业时的现实是——这么说暴露了我的年纪，28 年前——人们并不关注 IRR。

speaker: Unknown
en: People were like, focus on cash on cash return because IRR took care of itself.
zh: 人们当时都说,要关注现金回报率,因为 IRR 自然会照顾好自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in today's venture, the game has changed.
zh: 我觉得在如今的风投行业,游戏规则已经变了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to focus on IRR.
zh: 你必须关注 IRR。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know why?
zh: 你知道为什么吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because there's no way for venture to be successful in today's era without the Mag 7 participating in everything you're doing.
zh: 因为在今天这个时代,如果 Mag 7 不参与你做的每一件事,风投根本不可能成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every venture company is writing attacks to NVIDIA in some way, shape, or form, writing the attacks to a hyperscaler in some way, shape, or form, and possibly writing attacks to the foundational model in some way, type, or form.
zh: 每一家风投公司都在以某种方式、某种形式向 NVIDIA 写攻击,以某种方式、某种形式向超大规模云厂商写攻击,并且可能以某种方式、某种类型、某种形式向基础模型公司写攻击。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you're going to be successful, you're going to be writing attacks to all of them.
zh: 所以如果你想成功,你就得向所有这些公司写攻击。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of them are available in the public markets, or they will be soon in the public markets, for someone to invest in a no-fee, no-carry index fund.
zh: 而所有这些公司都可以在公开市场上买到,或者很快就会进入公开市场,供人们以零费用、零 carry 的指数基金形式投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you have to think about your IRR as, I've got to beat that with 1,000 basis points to justify anyone giving you capital in the private markets.
zh: 所以你必须把你的 IRR 想成:我必须比它高出 1000 个基点,才有理由让任何人在私募市场给你资本。

speaker: Unknown
en: You mentioned Town.
zh: 你提到了 Town。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had JD on the show.
zh: 我请过 JD 上我的节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really like him.
zh: 我很喜欢他。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've known him since the Plaid days.
zh: 我从 Plaid 时期就认识他了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm pissed off about that one because he started the company when he left.
zh: 那笔投资的事让我很恼火,因为他离开后就创办了公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember talking to him about it when he started.
zh: 我记得他刚创办的时候我和他聊过。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was doing something in some terrible space.
zh: 他当时在某个糟糕的领域做东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: No offense.
zh: 无意冒犯。

speaker: Unknown
en: He'll agree with me.
zh: 他会同意我的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he obviously pivoted.
zh: 然后他显然转型了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It taxed.
zh: 它 taxed 了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think they were doing something in tax and pivoted.
zh: 我记得他们当时在做税务方面的东西,然后转型了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm too old for this shit.
zh: 我干这行年纪太大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're a spring chicken.
zh: 你还是个毛头小伙。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for anyone watching, they'll see that you look much younger than me.
zh: 看节目的人会发现你看起来比我年轻多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But my question to you is, we obviously know what happened with the town round in terms of competitive nature and dynamics there.
zh: 但我的问题是,我们显然都知道 Town 那一轮在竞争性质和态势上发生了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't want to go into that.
zh: 我不想谈那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I want to go into is actually, does competition matter for VCs to invest against now?
zh: 我真正想谈的是,竞争现在对 VC 的投资还有影响吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: It seems like Andreessen has, you know, three companies all doing the same thing and many big platforms do.
zh: 看起来 Andreessen 有,你知道,三家公司都在做同一件事,很多大平台也是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does it matter being in many players in the same space anymore?
zh: 同一赛道有很多玩家,这还重要吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, this is a personal preference, right?
zh: 我的意思是,这是个人偏好问题,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think culturally for Matt, Sean, and I, you know, we like to be committed to the entrepreneur.
zh: 我认为从文化上讲,对 Matt、Sean 和我来说,我们喜欢对创业者保持承诺。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the situation has got to be, look, if we take a board seat and we write a big check, then we want to be.
zh: 而情况必须是,你看,如果我们拿下董事会席位、开出大额支票,那我们就想成为……

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's like, if you're investing the seed round and you have a small check, you're a passive investor, that's a different issue, right?
zh: 如果是,如果你投种子轮、支票很小,你是被动投资人,那是另一回事,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: But when we make a commitment to the entrepreneur, we want that to feel like a two-way commitment, right?
zh: 但当我们对创业者做出承诺时,我们希望那感觉上是一种双向承诺,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: We expect them to put the interest of their shareholders and commit to it.
zh: 我们期望他们把股东利益放在心上并为之投入。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we as shareholders need to commit to them.
zh: 而我们作为股东也需要对他们投入。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's why we didn't invest in OpenAI.
zh: 这就是我们没有投资 OpenAI 的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: We only stayed with Anthropic.
zh: 我们只留在了 Anthropic。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no shade.
zh: 没有贬低谁的意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, venture is changing in a way that multiple people are doing different things.
zh: 再说一次,风投正在发生变化,很多人在做不同的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you just have to figure out what is authentic to us and our values and live by those.
zh: 我认为你只需要弄清楚什么对我们、对我们的价值观来说是真诚的,并以此为准。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think for us, when we make a big commitment to the founder, we think of it as a two-way street.
zh: 而我认为对我们来说,当我们对创始人做出重大承诺时,我们把它看作一条双向道路。

speaker: Unknown
en: They commit to us, we commit to them.
zh: 他们对我们承诺,我们对他们承诺。

speaker: Unknown
en: One thing that we see a lot today is the compression and deployment timelines.
zh: 今天我们经常看到的一件事是部署时间线的压缩。

speaker: Unknown
en: In other words, people investing much faster.
zh: 换句话说,人们募资的速度快得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: All the LPs that I speak to are just saying, God, Harry, Jesus, everyone is coming back to market so much quicker, they're bigger.
zh: 我交谈过的所有 LP 都在说,天哪,Harry,老天,现在每个人都这么快回到市场,而且规模更大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that okay?
zh: 这没问题吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Or is that a sign of peak bubble?
zh: 还是这是泡沫见顶的信号?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it's very interesting.
zh: 是的,这非常有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: LPs want smaller funds, and then they want you to not come back quicker.
zh: LP 们想要更小的基金，然后又想让你不那么快回来募新基金。

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem is one of those can't be true.
zh: 问题是这两件事不可能同时成立。

speaker: Unknown
en: If the opportunity we have is real, and there's AI, the biggest economic platform in your lifetime, and you want smaller funds, then you're going to come back quicker.
zh: 如果我们面对的机会是真实的，而且有 AI——你一生中最大的经济平台——而你还想要更小的基金，那么你就会更快地回来募资。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, there are also large funds that are coming back quicker, so that's a different issue.
zh: 当然，也有一些大型基金更快地回来了，所以那是另一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think that the time we are in is one in which you're seeing companies grow so fast, and they need capital to grow.
zh: 但我认为我们所处的时代是一个公司增长如此之快的时代，而它们需要资本来增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, this is not a situation where you can grow without capital.
zh: 就是说，这不是一个没有资本也能增长的情境。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is not Google.
zh: 这不是 Google。

speaker: Unknown
en: Google, if you go back, probably raised less than 50 million in the private markets.
zh: 如果回顾 Google,它在私募市场可能总共募了不到 5000 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't do that today in AI.
zh: 今天在 AI 领域你不可能那么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need compute, you need to scale.
zh: 你需要算力，你需要规模化。

speaker: Unknown
en: So to me, because you're seeing them grow so fast, their capital needs are growing, and if a venture firm doesn't provide it, they're gonna get it from their competitors.
zh: 所以对我来说，因为你看到它们增长如此之快，它们的资本需求在增长，而如果一家风险投资机构不提供，它们就会从竞争对手那里拿到。

speaker: Unknown
en: So actually, if managers are deploying a fund in 18 months, LP should forgive them.
zh: 所以实际上，如果基金经理在 18 个月内就把一只基金投完，LP 应该谅解他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the LPs should ask questions and say, have you thought about it?
zh: 我认为 LP 应该提问：你有没有想过这个问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: How are you managing it?
zh: 你是怎么应对的？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's going to happen if things go?
zh: 如果事情发展下去会发生什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Vintage diversification does matter.
zh: 年份(vintage)多元化确实很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: People have to be conscious about that.
zh: 人们必须对此有意识。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I look at Menlo's history, the one fund that wasn't successful at Menlo's history, 50-year history, we only had one fund that's not returned capital, which is Menlo 8, which was invested in a 10-month period between 2000 and 2001.
zh: 回顾 Menlo 的历史，在 Menlo 50 年的历史中，唯一一只不成功的基金——我们只有一只没有返还资本的基金——就是 Menlo 8,它是在 2000 到 2001 年之间的 10 个月里投出去的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, that was not quite the outcome we wanted.
zh: 是啊，那不是我们想要的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: Menlo 8.
zh: Menlo 8。

speaker: Unknown
en: Menlo 8.
zh: Menlo 8。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I bring that up because I do think time diversification matters.
zh: 但我提这个是因为我确实认为时间多元化很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, by the way, Menlo 7 was one of the best funds in Menlo history.
zh: 顺便说一下，Menlo 7 可是 Menlo 历史上最好的基金之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, but do you remember Excel 2005, just pre the Facebook fund?
zh: 是啊，但你还记得 Excel 2005 吗，就在 Facebook 基金之前？

speaker: Unknown
en: And they had massive LP chain because they went and did a load of clean tech and bio, and it was not good.
zh: 他们遇到了大规模的 LP 链问题，因为他们跑去投了一堆清洁技术和生物科技，结果并不好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then Facebook fund.
zh: 然后就是 Facebook 基金。

speaker: Unknown
en: So to me, I just bring that up as like, look, as GPs, you've got to take the fiduciary duty you have to your LPs very seriously.
zh: 所以对我来说，我提这个只是想说：听着，作为 GP,你必须非常认真地对待你对 LP 负有的受托责任。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you've got to balance that decision.
zh: 你必须平衡那个决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I do know is that you can't just have dogmatic rules.
zh: 我所知道的是，你不能只有教条式的规则。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to play the game on the field.
zh: 你必须在球场上打球(因地制宜)。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you have to communicate what you're doing in a transparent way to your LPs and tell them what's happening.
zh: 然后你必须以透明的方式向你的 LP 沟通你在做什么，告诉他们正在发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And some LPs are going to be like, OK, I agree with you.
zh: 有些 LP 会说：好，我同意你。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to play it.
zh: 我想这么玩。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some people are not.
zh: 有些人则不会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you got to respect that.
zh: 你必须尊重这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the point is that you might have no choice to play the game this way.
zh: 但关键在于，你可能别无选择，只能以这种方式玩这场游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: Did you ever scale out of an LP class?
zh: 你有没有从一个 LP 类别中退出过？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I mean by that is, you know, the funds now are reasonably sized.
zh: 我的意思是，你知道，现在的基金规模还算合理。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're not egregiously sized.
zh: 并不是夸张的大。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, you're not David George asking for the U.S. Treasury, but you're $3 billion.
zh: 你知道，你不是 David George 那样向美国财政部要钱，但你是 30 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a lot of money.
zh: 这是很多钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: For some LPs, they're like, a lot.
zh: 对某些 LP 来说，他们会觉得：太多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Was there a time when you scaled out of endowments, say, and suddenly you had to be pension fund invested?
zh: 有没有一段时间你退出了，比如说，捐赠基金，突然之间你不得不依赖养老基金投资？

speaker: Unknown
en: We've historically, our anchor tenant has historically been the Washington State Investment Board, which is the Public Sector Pension Fund of the State of Washington, from RSLP, by the way.
zh: 从历史上看，我们的锚定出资人一直是华盛顿州投资委员会，也就是华盛顿州的公共部门养老基金，顺便说一句，来自 RSLP。

speaker: Unknown
en: I highly recommend them to anybody.
zh: 我强烈向任何人推荐他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've been our anchor tenants since 1981, so we have never had a reason
zh: 他们从 1981 年起就一直是我们的锚定出资人，所以我们从来没有理由

speaker: Unknown
en: To scale out because public sector pension funds have been a part.
zh: 退出，因为公共部门养老基金一直是其中的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a little bit of a cultural dynamic.
zh: 这有一点文化上的因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the founders of Menlo came from very humble beginnings.
zh: 我认为 Menlo 的创始人出身非常平凡。

speaker: Unknown
en: They both grew up in a house with no running water or toilets.
zh: 他们俩都是在没有自来水、没有厕所的房子里长大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think John was orphaned very early.
zh: 我认为 John 很早就成了孤儿。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was a scholarship student at MIT.
zh: 他是 MIT 的奖学金学生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so they love the idea of working for public sector employees because that felt like working for their parents and less these people look more like their parents and their children.
zh: 所以他们很喜欢为公共部门员工工作的想法，因为那感觉像是为自己的父母工作，而且这些人看起来更像是他们的父母和他们的孩子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Love that.
zh: 喜欢这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there wasn't a fund where LPs went, oh, Venki, you're getting pretty big now.
zh: 所以并没有 LP 跑来说，哦，Venki，你现在规模已经相当大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you're just scaling out of our sweet spot.
zh: 我觉得你已经快超出我们的舒适区了。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, that wasn't the case, but we raised that first billion dollar fund in venture capital.
zh: 不，没有那种情况，但我们确实募集了第一支十亿美元的创投基金。

speaker: Unknown
en: Menlo 9, which was raised in 2001, was a $1.5 billion fund, and Menlo 10, which was raised in 2004, was a $1.2 billion fund.
zh: Menlo 9，于 2001 年募集，是一只 15 亿美元的基金，Menlo 10，于 2004 年募集，是一只 12 亿美元的基金。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those funds did not perform as well as we would have liked, and many LPs did leave us.
zh: 那些基金的表现不如我们期望的那样好，许多 LP 确实离开了我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: You manage a lot of the LP conversations today, correct?
zh: 你今天负责很多 LP 的沟通，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I do.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Matt and I do a lot of them, yes.
zh: 我和 Matt 负责其中很多，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you hear from them?
zh: 你从他们那里听到什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: As I said, I hear deployment time is down, in terms of how people are investing much faster, and the funds are just getting bigger.
zh: 正如我所说，我听到的是部署时间在下降，也就是人们的投资速度快了很多，而且基金规模越来越大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I also just see mimicry, which is like, I'm calling this out because it's a compliment to her.
zh: 然后我还看到了模仿，我之所以提这一点，是因为这是对她的一种赞美。

speaker: Unknown
en: I never shit down on people, other than your piece.

en: And you said, I appreciate your leadership through the woke times.

speaker: Unknown
en: And to me, I think that's the most important, to try to be authentic to who you are.

zh: 而且他有员工离开了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think he ultimately said, we want people who are authentic to Coinbase values, articulated by me, the founder.
zh: 但我想他最终说的是，我们想要的是对我、也就是创始人所阐述的 Coinbase 价值观保持真实的人。

en: Have you ever been inauthentic to who you are?
zh: 你有没有过对自己不真实的时刻？

en: I think there are times when, you know, you say certain things to founders because you want them to like you or you want to win a deal that may not be truly authentic.
zh: 我想有些时候，你知道，你会对创始人说某些话，是因为你想让他们喜欢你，或者你想赢下一笔交易，而这些话可能并不是真正真实的。

en: What I'll tell you is that I have dealt with my own insecurities and feeling like an imposter.
zh: 我能告诉你的是，我曾经面对过自己的不安全感和冒名顶替的感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've gotten more comfortable in my skin now where I just feel like I just don't do it.
zh: 而我现在对自己的状态自在多了，我就是觉得我不再那样做了。 [[904/905 之间无内容]]

speaker: Unknown
en: And if it means I have to say something inauthentic to me to win the deal, I'd rather not win it.
zh: 如果意味着我必须说不真实于自己的话才能赢下交易，那我宁愿不赢。

zh: 但这么说很容易，因为我已经到了人生中“赢”不重要的阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: What would be your single biggest piece of advice to an LP allocating into venture in this time?
zh: 你会给在这个时期配置资金到风险投资的 LP 一个什么最重要的建议？

speaker: Unknown
en: Look at the windshield, not the rear view mirror.
zh: 看挡风玻璃，别看后视镜。

speaker: Unknown
en: The results and financial performance are rear view mirror calculations, and they're good about telling you what they did in the past.
zh: 业绩和财务表现是后视镜式的计算，它们很擅长告诉你他们过去做了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't tell you how some of a firm's going to do.
zh: 它们不会告诉你一家机构未来会做得怎么样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Performance is a lagging indicator, and it's actually a five to seven year lagging indicator.
zh: 业绩是一个滞后指标，而且实际上是一个滞后五到七年的指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: So my advice would be call a bunch of entrepreneurs or successful AI companies and ask them who are the partners they respect.
zh: 所以我的建议是，打电话给一批成功的 AI 公司的创业者，问他们尊敬哪些合伙人。

speaker: Unknown
en: In my email, they didn't take the money.
zh: 在我的邮件里，他们没有拿这笔钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if the firm you're talking to doesn't have a few of those partners in the mix, then that's your windshield.
zh: 如果你正在谈的机构里没有几个这样的合伙人，那才是你的挡风玻璃。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you stop your team getting arrogant?
zh: 你怎么防止你的团队变得傲慢？

speaker: Unknown
en: You guys have got the winning hand.
zh: 你们手里握着一把稳赢的牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're only as good as your last investment.
zh: 你只和你上一笔投资一样好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't matter if you're the lion or the antelope in the savannah.
zh: 无论你是狮子还是羚羊，在草原上都一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: You wake up in the morning if you're the lion.
zh: 如果你是狮子，你早上醒来。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you don't run, you don't eat.
zh: 你不跑，就没得吃。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're the antelope, you don't run, you don't live.
zh: 如果你是羚羊，你不跑，就没命。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just have to run.
zh: 你就是得跑。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like you have to think about the most important meeting is the next one.
zh: 我觉得你必须这么想：最重要的会议是下一场。

speaker: Unknown
en: The most important investment is the next one.
zh: 最重要的投资是下一笔。

speaker: Unknown
en: The most important board meeting is the next one.
zh: 最重要的董事会是下一场。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you don't spend time in the present thinking about it, I think you lose this game.
zh: 如果你不花时间在当下思考这些，我认为你就会输掉这场游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the secret to marriage when you scale wealth over time together?
zh: 当你们一起随着时间积累财富时，婚姻的秘诀是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, wow.
zh: 哦，哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, you got to marry someone better than you, which I did.
zh: 嗯,你得娶一个比你更好的人,我就做到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you got to convince her to stay with you or him, whatever your preference might be.
zh: 然后你得说服她愿意和你在一起,或者和他,取决于你的偏好是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Finding a life partner who inspires you to be the best version of yourself and supports you to be that is, I think, critical.
zh: 找到一个能激励你成为最好的自己、并支持你成为那样的伴侣,我认为至关重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we can do that for each other, I think that'll because I think at the core of a long term marriage is, I think, real respect.
zh: 如果我们能为彼此做到这一点,我认为那会——因为我认为长期婚姻的核心,是真正的尊重。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's love and real respect, but I think respect is super important, and that comes from inspiring each other to be the best version of you can be.
zh: 是爱和真正的尊重,但我认为尊重极其重要,而它来自于激励彼此成为你能成为的最好版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the best advice you've ever been given?
zh: 你得到过的最好建议是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: You mentioned Mr. Steve Sloan and his father-in-law.
zh: 你提到了 Steve Sloan 先生和他的岳父。

speaker: Unknown
en: His father-in-law is one of my greatest friends, and he once said to me, you're never wrong to do the right thing, but the right thing is very often the hard thing.
zh: 他的岳父是我最好的朋友之一,他曾对我说,做对的事你永远不会错,但对的事往往是最难的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think the best advice I've gotten, I've really centered around people.
zh: 是的,我得到过的最好建议,我认为都围绕着人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that Ronald Reagan has a quote that Tom Riley, who was a CEO of Trico, told me, wanted to do that.
zh: 我认为罗纳德·里根有一句话,是 Trico 的 CEO Tom Riley 告诉我的,想这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no limit to what a person can do as long as you don't care who gets the credit.
zh: 只要你不在乎谁获得功劳,一个人能做的事就没有极限。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have felt when I was early in my career, I was very focused on getting credit.
zh: 我在职业生涯早期,非常执着于获得功劳。

speaker: Unknown
en: I really, like, am I going to get credit?
zh: 我真的,比如说,我会得到功劳吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I have let go of that and focused on just doing what's right and not worrying about if I'm going to get credit.
zh: 后来我放下了这一点,专注于做正确的事,而不去担心我是否会得到功劳。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's actually been pretty freeing, and I think that's made me a better teammate.
zh: 这其实让人非常解脱,我认为这让我成为一个更好的队友。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that.
zh: 我很喜欢这句话。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think there's a better way to end than on that.
zh: 我不认为有比这更好的结尾方式了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your humility is astonishing.
zh: 你的谦逊令人惊叹。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really just like, one, you're very calming.
zh: 真的就像,第一,你让人非常平静。

speaker: Unknown
en: I almost feel like you should be like on Headspace or calm, one.
zh: 我几乎觉得你应该上 Headspace 或者 Calm 之类的节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: And two, it's just a wonderful humility that I rarely see as a venture investor.
zh: 第二,这是一种我作为风险投资人很少见到的美好谦逊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much for doing this, Amir.
zh: 非常感谢你来做这期节目,Amir。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have too many successful people on your show.
zh: 你的节目上成功人士太多了。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我试着帮你降低一下门槛。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've so enjoyed this.
zh: 我非常享受这次对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for doing it.
zh: 谢谢你来做这期节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you see shows like this, why it's so much better in person?
zh: 你看,像这样的节目,为什么现场要精彩得多?

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't have this virtue, so thank you for doing it.
zh: 你没法有这种效果,所以感谢你来做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you, Harry, and thank you for... Look, I have to say, my colleague Claire was coming with me and she said, I watch Harry all the time.
zh: 谢谢你,Harry,也谢谢你……听着,我必须说,我的同事 Claire 本来要和我一起来,她说,我一直看 Harry 的节目。

speaker: Unknown
